body.statement: There are constants depending only on \((c_-,c_+,\kappa,\lambda_0)\) such that, uniformly over \(\mathcal M_n\) and \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_0\), \(P\{e(X)\le\lambda\}\asymp\lambda^{\kappa}\) and \(E_P[(e(X)\vee\lambda)^{-1}]\asymp v_{\kappa}(\lambda)^2\), where \(v_{\kappa}(\lambda)=\lambda^{-(1-\kappa)/2}\) for \(0<\kappa<1\), \(v_1(\lambda)=\sqrt{1+\log(\lambda_0/\lambda)}\), and \(v_{\kappa}(\lambda)=1\) for \(\kappa>1\).
body.justification: This converts the primitive dyadic law into the two class-uniform tail functionals used on both sides of the frontier.
body.gap: KhanTamer2010Irregular provides tail-rate intuition but not this uniform dyadic-shell equivalence for the present law--function class.
body.consumer: The clipped-score upper bound and every shell-localized lower family use these comparisons.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \((P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\mathcal M_n\) and
\(0<\lambda\leq\lambda_0\).  By \texttt{ass:positivity},
\[
\{0<e(X)\leq\lambda\}
=\mathop{\dot\bigcup}_{j=0}^{\infty}
\{2^{-j-1}\lambda<e(X)\leq2^{-j}\lambda\}
\quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
The upper half of \texttt{ass:uniform-shell} and countable additivity give
\[
P\{e(X)\leq\lambda\}
\leq c_+\lambda^\kappa\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}2^{-j\kappa}
={c_+\over1-2^{-\kappa}}\lambda^\kappa.
\]
The shell with upper endpoint \(\lambda\) and the lower half of the same
assumption give
\[
P\{e(X)\leq\lambda\}
\geq P\{\lambda/2<e(X)\leq\lambda\}
\geq c_-\lambda^\kappa.
\]
This proves the first uniform equivalence and states explicitly where positivity
is used.

Put \(H_\lambda=E_P[(e(X)\vee\lambda)^{-1}]\).  The part below \(\lambda\)
satisfies
\[
c_-\lambda^{\kappa-1}
\leq {P\{e(X)\leq\lambda\}\over\lambda}
\leq {c_+\over1-2^{-\kappa}}\lambda^{\kappa-1}.             \tag{1}
\]
Let \(J\) be the largest nonnegative integer for which
\(2^J\lambda\leq\lambda_0\).  For \(0\leq j<J\), on the shell
\(2^j\lambda<e(X)\leq2^{j+1}\lambda\), inverse propensity is at most
\((2^j\lambda)^{-1}\), and the upper shell bound at
\(2^{j+1}\lambda\) yields
\[
E_P\!\left[
{\mathbf 1\{2^j\lambda<e(X)\leq2^{j+1}\lambda\}\over e(X)}
\right]
\leq2c_+(2^{j+1}\lambda)^{\kappa-1}.                       \tag{2}
\]
On the terminal event \(e(X)>2^J\lambda\), inverse propensity is at most
\((2^J\lambda)^{-1}<2/\lambda_0\).  Consequently
\[
H_\lambda\leq C\left[1+\lambda^{\kappa-1}
\sum_{j=0}^{J-1}2^{j(\kappa-1)}\right],                       \tag{3}
\]
where an empty sum is zero.  If \(0<\kappa<1\), the geometric sum in (3) is
bounded, and (1) gives \(H_\lambda\asymp\lambda^{\kappa-1}\).  If
\(\kappa=1\), every complete shell between \(\lambda\) and \(\lambda_0\)
contributes at least
\[
{1\over2^{j+1}\lambda}
P\{2^j\lambda<e(X)\leq2^{j+1}\lambda\}\geq {c_-\over2},
\]
while (2) gives a constant upper contribution per shell.  The number of
complete shells, together with the contribution below \(\lambda\), is
comparable to \(1+\log(\lambda_0/\lambda)\); hence
\(H_\lambda\asymp1+\log(\lambda_0/\lambda)\).  If \(\kappa>1\), the sum in
(3), after multiplication by \(\lambda^{\kappa-1}\), is uniformly bounded,
whereas the fixed top shell gives
\[
H_\lambda\geq\lambda_0^{-1}
P\{\lambda_0/2<e(X)\leq\lambda_0\}
\geq c_-\lambda_0^{\kappa-1}.
\]
These cases are exactly \(H_\lambda\asymp v_\kappa(\lambda)^2\).  Every
comparison constant is independent of \(P\), \(n\), and \(\lambda\).
